crypto_call_justification: seed-scan implements no cryptographic primitive. It calls hashlib's sha256 and the ssl module from the standard library, and takes the mnemonic schemes, the derivation and the addresses from bip39-slip39, bip32-descriptors, btclib-wallet, coin-addresses and btclib, the packages built for them; git grep -E 'hmac|pbkdf|ecdsa|keccak|secp|scrypt|ripemd' -- src/ finds nothing. bundle.py decodes Base58Check itself, an encoding whose checksum it takes from hashlib's sha256. https://github.com/btclib-org/seed-scan/blob/main/pyproject.toml
crypto_certificate_verification_justific: Every TLS connection verifies the certificate, by default and with no option that turns it off. The context of the Electrum server scan and forks ask is ssl.create_default_context, which requires a certificate chaining to a trusted CA and naming the host, against the system's CA certificates or those of the file --cafile names alone (cli._tls_context). The Ethereum node over https is verified against the system's CA certificates and must name the host (seed_scan.evm). --tcp, the user's explicit option, uses no TLS at all: it reaches an Electrum server on loopback alone, neither encrypted nor authenticated, as README.md and SECURITY.md say, and --cafile is refused with it. tests/scan_cli_test.py asserts CERT_REQUIRED and check_hostname on every Electrum context, and refuses a server or a node whose certificate does not verify. https://github.com/btclib-org/seed-scan/blob/main/src/seed_scan/cli.py
crypto_credential_agility_justification: seed-scan supports no file for a credential or a private key, by design: the mnemonic and the passphrases, from which every key is derived, are read at a hidden prompt alone, and cli.py refuses to read them from an argument, a file, standard input or the environment, so that a secret never rests where the process list, the shell's history or the disk keep it. It writes only to standard output and standard error, and reads the files the user names and the system's CA certificates: ssl.create_default_context() for the Electrum server without --cafile, and load_default_certs() in the node's context. https://github.com/btclib-org/seed-scan/blob/main/src/seed_scan/cli.py
crypto_floss_justification: Every cryptographic function it uses is FLOSS: CPython's hashlib and ssl over OpenSSL, and the MIT-licensed btclib-org packages it depends on, with pyca/cryptography beneath btclib-wallet. https://github.com/btclib-org/seed-scan/blob/main/pyproject.toml
crypto_keylength_justification: The keys it derives are fixed by their schemes, secp256k1 keys of 256 bits, and the hash it calls is SHA-256. TLS takes CPython's default context, which refuses TLS below 1.2 and offers no cipher below 128-bit strength (get_ciphers, measured 2026-11-14). No option selects a shorter key. https://github.com/btclib-org/seed-scan/blob/main/src/seed_scan/cli.py
crypto_password_storage_justification: seed-scan stores no password and authenticates no user. A BIP39 passphrase typed at the prompt is used to derive a seed and never stored.
crypto_pfs_justification: The only key agreement is TLS's, and every cipher CPython's default TLS client context offers agrees keys with ECDHE or DHE, or is TLS 1.3's, which is always ephemeral (ssl.SSLContext(ssl.PROTOCOL_TLS_CLIENT).get_ciphers(), measured 2026-11-14).
crypto_published_justification: Every algorithm is a published one: SHA-256 (FIPS 180-4), the BIP39, SLIP-0039 and Electrum mnemonic schemes, BIP32 derivation on secp256k1, and TLS 1.2 and 1.3. identify's tests run a vector its authors publish for each scheme it reads (tests/no_secret_test.py). https://github.com/btclib-org/seed-scan/blob/main/README.md#identifying-a-mnemonic
crypto_random_justification: seed-scan generates no key and no nonce of its own: nothing under src/ imports random or secrets or reads os.urandom. The keys and nonces of its TLS connections are OpenSSL's, drawn from OpenSSL's CSPRNG. https://github.com/btclib-org/seed-scan/blob/main/src/seed_scan/
crypto_tls12_justification: Every TLS connection requires TLS 1.2 at least. The Electrum context scan and forks share sets minimum_version to TLSv1_2 (cli._tls_context), which tests/scan_cli_test.py asserts. The node's context is an ssl.SSLContext(PROTOCOL_TLS_CLIENT), whose minimum is TLS 1.2 on CPython 3.11 and 3.15, the floor requires-python sets and the newest the classifiers name (measured 2026-11-14). https://github.com/btclib-org/seed-scan/blob/main/src/seed_scan/cli.py
crypto_used_network_justification: Every connection is encrypted unless the user asks for plain text on the machine itself. The Electrum servers of scan and forks are reached over TLS or, with --tcp, the user's explicit option, over plain TCP to a host that resolves to loopback addresses alone, 127.0.0.0/8 or ::1, any other being refused; README.md and SECURITY.md say that connection is not encrypted or authenticated. The Ethereum node is reached over https, and over plain http only at a host written as a loopback IP address, such as 127.0.0.1 or [::1]: seed_scan.evm refuses http to any other host, a name such as localhost included. No server or node is asked unless the user names it. https://github.com/btclib-org/seed-scan/blob/main/src/seed_scan/cli.py
crypto_verification_private_justificatio: No HTTP header seed-scan sends carries private information. Its only HTTP requests are those to the Ethereum node, which set Content-Type beside what Python's HTTP client adds, and a node URL carrying a login is refused, so no credential is sent; seed-scan sends no cookie. Over https the certificate is verified in the TLS handshake, before any request is sent, so the addresses asked, which tie a wallet's accounts together, travel only after it. The Electrum protocol, over TLS or over --tcp, sends no HTTP headers. https://github.com/btclib-org/seed-scan/blob/main/src/seed_scan/evm.py
crypto_weaknesses_justification: No SHA-1 or MD5 appears under src/: hashlib is called for sha256 alone, and CPython's default TLS context excludes SHA-1 cipher suites. https://github.com/btclib-org/seed-scan/blob/main/src/seed_scan/

hardening_justification: identify and report add an audit hook that refuses every socket and every new process before they read anything, and refuse to run where the hook is not in place, so that a defect in the package or a dependency cannot send the mnemonic or the bundle anywhere. scan and forks verify certificates with TLS 1.2 at least, bound every answer they read, refuse plain http but at a host written as a loopback IP address, and refuse --tcp, the user's explicit option for plain TCP, to a host that does not resolve to loopback addresses alone. https://github.com/btclib-org/seed-scan/blob/main/src/seed_scan/cli.py
implement_secure_design_justification: The design keeps the secret on one machine: identify reads it and opens no connection, scan and forks read only public data, and report reads them offline (README.md's *What touches the secret*). Defaults fail safe: no server or node is asked unless the user names it, certificates are verified, plain TCP to an Electrum server is used only under --tcp and refused off loopback, plain http is refused but at a host written as a loopback IP address, scan and forks refuse a server whose genesis block or whose blocks at the checkpoints of the chain read are not that chain's, and a bundle, a scan result or a forks result of another format or version is refused, and so is a result made from another bundle. An audit hook mediates every socket and process in identify and report. https://github.com/btclib-org/seed-scan/blob/main/README.md#what-touches-the-secret
input_validation_justification: Every input from outside is checked against its format and refused otherwise, with a SeedScanTypeError or SeedScanValueError: seed_scan.bundle.loads, seed_scan.scan.loads and seed_scan.forks.loads refuse text that is not JSON, another format or version, a missing member or one of the wrong type, and hold each text member to the values the format defines; seed_scan.evm refuses a node answer that is not a JSON-RPC 2.0 response or a bounded quantity, and, before the node is asked, an address that is not 0x and 40 hex digits in one case or in its EIP-55 checksum case; the server is parsed as host:port. tests/scan_loads_test.py, tests/forks_loads_test.py, tests/bundle_test.py and tests/evm_test.py hold them; a test driving the rule over every public function is owed by btclib-org/seed-scan#3. https://github.com/btclib-org/seed-scan/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md#the-public-surface
